material: Aluminium body with a tempered-glass touchscreen
features: Built-in Wi-Fi at $80 — the V1 was Bluetooth-only
AI self-learning fingerprint sensor, ~0.5s reads
Up to 50 access codes with anti-peep entry
USB-C emergency power contact plus a keyed cylinder
No subscription for remote unlock, codes or history

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Listed as BHMA Grade 2 on retail listings; Wyze does not publish a certification number or ANSI standard reference
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — the exterior cylinder and keys are replaced
specs.smartRadio: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built into the lock. No Matter, no Thread, no Z-Wave
specs.hubRequired: No — the Wi-Fi radio is in the lock itself
specs.biometrics: Fingerprint, up to 50 prints stored on the lock
specs.backupAccess: Physical key cylinder plus a USB-C emergency power port on the exterior
specs.doorFit: Standard US single-cylinder deadbolt prep; Wyze does not publish a door-thickness or backset range

pros: The cheapest lock here with genuine built-in Wi-Fi — no bridge, no hub, no subscription
Fingerprint reader is the standout: reviewers report sub-second, weather-tolerant reads
Keyed cylinder AND a USB-C emergency contact, which several $300 locks here do not both have
IP53-rated and runs 8 months on eight cheap AA cells
cons: No Matter, no Thread, no Apple Home — it lives inside the Wyze app and Alexa/Google, and that is the whole ecosystem
The BHMA Grade 2 claim appears only on retail listings; Wyze publishes no certification listing to check it against
Eight AA batteries is a lot of dead weight and a lot of cells to buy
Wyze's history of app outages and security incidents is a real consideration for a device that guards your front door
shortTagline: Real Wi-Fi and a fast fingerprint reader for $80 — the ecosystem is the compromise.

model: SwitchBot Lock Pro + Hub Mini (Matter Enabled) bundle
features: Bolts over the inside thumbturn — nothing on the outside of the door changes
Bundled Hub Mini Matter Enabled is what actually provides Matter and remote access
4 x AA cells instead of the CR123A cells the older SwitchBot Lock used
Fits single deadbolts, jimmy-proof and (with an adapter) mortise locks
Optional rechargeable Dual Power Pack replaces the AAs

specs.lockType: Retrofit over the existing deadbolt's interior thumbturn
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Not applicable and not published — a retrofit motor carries no BHMA grade, and your door keeps whatever grade its existing deadbolt already had
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: Yes — the original exterior cylinder and keys are untouched
specs.smartRadio: Bluetooth only inside the lock. SwitchBot states plainly: 'Lock Pro is not directly Matter enabled'
specs.hubRequired: Yes — and it is included in this bundle. Without a SwitchBot Hub Mini Matter Enabled or Hub 2 there is no Matter, no remote access and no voice control
specs.biometrics: None in this bundle — fingerprint requires the separate Keypad Touch or Keypad Vision
specs.batteryType: 4 x AA (included); optional rechargeable Dual Power Pack
specs.backupAccess: Your existing exterior key always works; SwitchBot describes a triple-power design (main, backup and emergency)
specs.doorFit: Works with most US single deadbolts, jimmy-proof and mortise locks (adapter); no drilling and no new bore

pros: The most landlord-proof install here: no drilling, no new hardware outside, fully reversible
Your existing key keeps working, which matters when the battery dies at 11pm
AA cells rather than CR123A — SwitchBot's own figure is roughly a third of the battery cost of the old Lock
The bundle includes the hub, so Matter works out of the box rather than after a second purchase
cons: The lock is Bluetooth-only. Every remote feature, every Matter integration and every voice command runs through the hub — lose the hub and you have a Bluetooth thumbturn
No keypad or fingerprint in this bundle; adding Keypad Touch or Keypad Vision is another $60-$180
Retrofit means your security is still whatever your existing deadbolt was — an ungraded builder-grade lock stays ungraded
Bolted to the inside of the door, it is visibly a gadget rather than a lock
shortTagline: The renter's answer: keeps your keyway, but the lock itself is Bluetooth-only.

material: Metal lock body with a separate polycarbonate keypad unit
features: Retrofit body plus a wireless exterior keypad, both in the box
Apple Home Key over NFC on a retrofit lock — still rare
USB-C rechargeable lithium pack in the lock body
Adapter kits for US deadbolts and several European profiles
Fingerprint and PIN entry live on the keypad, not the lock

specs.lockType: Retrofit over the existing deadbolt, plus a separate wireless keypad
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Not published by the manufacturer — Aqara says only 'BHMA-certified' on the U-series pages without naming a grade or standard
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: Yes — the exterior cylinder and your keys stay in place
specs.smartRadio: Matter over Thread plus Bluetooth. No Wi-Fi anywhere in the product
specs.hubRequired: Yes — a Thread border router per ecosystem (HomePod mini, HomePod 2, Apple TV 4K, or equivalent). Without one there is no remote access and no Home Key
specs.appleHomeKey: Yes, over NFC at the keypad
specs.biometrics: Fingerprint, on the exterior keypad unit
specs.batteryType: Rechargeable lithium pack in the lock (USB-C); keypad takes 4 x AAA or 12-24V DC wiring
specs.backupAccess: Your existing exterior key still works; USB-C on the lock body accepts a power bank
specs.doorFit: Standard US single-cylinder deadbolts via the included adapters; slim-profile US deadbolts may need replacing first, and the keypad must sit within about 6 ft (2 m) of the lock

pros: Apple Home Key, fingerprint and Matter over Thread on a retrofit that keeps your existing keyway — nothing else here does all four
Thread sips power, and the lock body recharges over USB-C rather than eating AA cells
Works across Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, SmartThings and Home Assistant through Matter rather than a proprietary cloud
Keypad is wireless, so it can be mounted away from the door frame if your deadbolt prep is awkward
cons: No Thread border router means no remote control, no Home Key and no smart-home integration — the hub is not in the box and is not optional
Aqara says 'BHMA-certified' but publishes no grade, so you cannot compare its security to a Grade 1 Schlage or Level
Long-run reliability is the weak point: the Amazon listing sits at 2.7 stars across ~2,000 ratings, with owners reporting jamming and grinding after a year or so
Two batteries to manage — a rechargeable pack in the lock and AAAs in the keypad — with different lives
shortTagline: Home Key and Thread on a retrofit — provided you already own a Thread border router.

material: Zinc alloy body with a capacitive touch keypad
features: Built-in 2.4GHz Wi-Fi — no eufy HomeBase or bridge needed
Fingerprint, keypad, app, key and voice entry
USB-C emergency power contact on the exterior escutcheon
Fingerprint templates stored on the lock rather than in eufy's cloud
No subscription for remote unlock or history

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: ANSI/BHMA Grade 3 — the lowest of the three residential grades (PCWorld's review states Level 3 on the three-point scale)
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — the exterior cylinder and keys are replaced
specs.smartRadio: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built in; Matter over Thread is advertised
specs.hubRequired: No for the eufy app. Matter needs a Thread border router — and PCWorld could not get Matter pairing to complete on an Apple TV 4K or a SmartThings Station
specs.biometrics: Fingerprint reader; PCWorld's reviewer described it as finicky
specs.backupAccess: Physical key cylinder plus a USB-C emergency power port on the exterior
specs.doorFit: Standard US single-cylinder deadbolt prep; eufy does not publish a door-thickness range

pros: Wi-Fi is genuinely in the lock — you are not buying a bridge afterwards, unlike most of eufy's older C-series
Both fallbacks covered: a keyed cylinder and a USB-C emergency contact
Fingerprints are held on the device, not uploaded, and eufy charges no subscription for lock features
Eight months on AA cells with no proprietary battery pack to source later
cons: ANSI/BHMA Grade 3 — the weakest residential grade, and a real step down from the Grade 1 locks at $250-$350 here
The Matter support on the box did not work in PCWorld's testing across two different Thread hubs; treat it as unproven rather than a feature
No Apple Home Key, so iPhone users get app control but not tap-to-unlock
The fingerprint reader is the least reliable of the biometric locks in this set
shortTagline: Cheap built-in Wi-Fi and fingerprint, undermined by a Grade 3 body and shaky Matter.

model: Yale Approach Lock with Wi-Fi + Keypad
material: Polycarbonate lock body with a separate touchscreen keypad
connectivity: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi (via the included Connect Wi-Fi Bridge)
features: Replaces the inside thumbturn only — the outside of the door is unchanged
Connect Wi-Fi Bridge is in the box on this SKU, not an add-on
12-month claimed life on 4 x AA in the lock; 7 months on 4 x AAA in the keypad
Runs on the Yale Home / August app with shared guest access and history
Yale says Matter support will arrive by software update

specs.lockType: Retrofit over the existing deadbolt's interior thumbturn, plus a separate keypad
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Not published by the manufacturer — Yale states no ANSI/BHMA grade for the Approach, and the retrofit inherits the grade of your existing deadbolt
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: Yes — that is the point of the product; your existing cylinder and keys stay
specs.smartRadio: Bluetooth in the lock and keypad. Wi-Fi comes from the plug-in Connect Bridge, which is included on this bundle
specs.hubRequired: Yes, but included — the Connect Wi-Fi Bridge is what provides remote access. The cheaper Approach SKUs omit it and Tom's Guide flags that as their main caveat
specs.biometrics: Sources conflict: Yale's own bundle page lists the fingerprint-capable Keypad Touch, while the Amazon listing for this bundle describes a code-only Bluetooth touchscreen keypad. Confirm which keypad ships before ordering
specs.batteryType: Lock: 4 x AA alkaline (included). Keypad: 4 x AAA alkaline (included)
specs.backupAccess: Your existing exterior key always works; Yale does not publish an emergency power contact on the Approach
specs.doorFit: Most single-cylinder deadbolts; the keypad mounts within about 30 ft of the lock over Bluetooth. Lock body is 2.6 x 5.6 x 1.6 in on the inside of the door

pros: The bridge is actually in the box at this price, which is not true of the cheaper Approach listings buyers usually land on
12 months of claimed lock battery life is the longest AA figure in this set
Keeps your keyway and your keys, so nothing about the outside of your door changes
Backed by Yale/August's mature app, which is markedly better maintained than most budget lock apps
cons: No Matter today — Yale describes it as coming by software update, which is a promise rather than a feature you can buy
No Apple Home Key and no HomeKit tap-to-unlock; iPhone owners are in the Yale app
Yale publishes no ANSI/BHMA grade, and a retrofit cannot improve the deadbolt you already have
Which keypad you get is genuinely unclear between Yale's own listing and the Amazon listing — fingerprint or code-only changes the value considerably
shortTagline: A retrofit with the Wi-Fi bridge actually included — and no Matter yet.

model: August Wi-Fi Smart Lock (4th Gen, AUG-SL05)
features: Dual-band Wi-Fi built into the lock — no August Connect bridge required
45% smaller than the 3rd-gen August it replaced
DoorSense magnetic sensor tells you the door is actually shut, not just locked
Retrofit over your existing deadbolt; your keys keep working
Apple HomeKit, Alexa and Google Assistant support

specs.lockType: Retrofit over the existing deadbolt's interior thumbturn
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Not applicable and not published — the retrofit motor carries no BHMA grade and your existing deadbolt keeps its own
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: Yes — the exterior cylinder and your keys are untouched
specs.smartRadio: 802.11 b/g/n Wi-Fi on both 2.4GHz and 5GHz, plus Bluetooth, all inside the lock
specs.hubRequired: No — this is the generation that moved Wi-Fi into the lock body. Older August locks needed the separate Connect bridge
specs.appleHomeKey: No — HomeKit control only, not tap-to-unlock
specs.biometrics: None — there is no keypad and no fingerprint reader in the box
specs.backupAccess: Your existing exterior key always works; August does not publish an emergency power contact on this generation
specs.doorFit: Most single-cylinder deadbolts — check August's compatibility list first. Body is 72mm across and 46mm deep on the inside of the door

pros: The only retrofit here with dual-band Wi-Fi in the lock — it will join a 5GHz-only guest network that defeats most rivals
DoorSense is still the best-implemented door-ajar sensor in the category
Mature HomeKit support and an app that has had a decade of iteration
Retrofit install takes minutes and is fully reversible for renters
cons: August's own figure is up to 3 months of battery life, and owners routinely report changing the CR123A cells every 90 days — by far the worst battery economics here
CR123A cells cost several times what AAs do, so the running cost is real
No keypad, no fingerprint, no Home Key: without your phone you are back to the metal key
No Matter support has been published for this generation, and it is a 2020 design at a 2026 price
shortTagline: Best-in-class retrofit hardware, sabotaged by roughly 3 months per set of CR123A cells.

material: Metal escutcheon with a capacitive keypad
features: One of the first Matter-over-Thread locks with a fingerprint reader
Up to 100 fingerprints (two per user) and 50 passcodes
Magnetic door sensor included for open/closed status
18-month electronics warranty, longer than most rivals here
Thread instead of Wi-Fi, for markedly longer battery life

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: ANSI/BHMA Grade 1 per U-tec's marketing and review coverage; U-tec does not publish a certification listing number, and its Bolt-series pages elsewhere say only 'tested to BHMA and ANSI standards'
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — the exterior cylinder and keys are replaced
specs.smartRadio: Matter over Thread plus Bluetooth. There is no Wi-Fi radio in the lock
specs.hubRequired: Yes — a Thread border router for Matter, or U-tec's own Wi-Fi Bridge (sold separately) if you want the Xthings/U-Home app to work remotely
specs.appleHomeKey: No — U-tec confirms no NFC tap-to-unlock on the Bolt series
specs.uwbUnlock: No — that is the dearer Bolt Mission
specs.biometrics: Fingerprint, up to 100 prints (2 per user)
specs.backupAccess: Physical key cylinder included; U-tec does not publish an emergency power contact for this model
specs.doorFit: Standard US doors. Explicitly not for glass doors, sliding doors, mortise locks or multi-point locks

pros: Thread rather than Wi-Fi: U-tec claims up to a year in Matter mode and two years on Bluetooth, and reviewers back the long-life claim
Fingerprint plus Matter at $200 is a combination the big brands still charge $300+ for
18-month electronics warranty is the longest in this group
Matter setup into Apple Home is a QR scan — no proprietary cloud account needed for the smart-home half
cons: No Apple Home Key at all, so iPhone owners lose the single best reason to buy a Matter lock
The 'ANSI Grade 1' claim comes from marketing and reviews, not from a published certification listing you can verify
Remote access in U-tec's own app needs the separately sold Wi-Fi Bridge; Matter alone needs a Thread border router. Either way there is a second box
Reviewers consistently flag a loud motor, fiddly fingerprint enrolment and a flaky auto-lock timer
shortTagline: Fingerprint plus Matter-over-Thread at $200 — but no Home Key and no hub in the box.

material: Metal escutcheon with a capacitive touchscreen
features: Both Wi-Fi and Matter-over-Thread radios on board — you pick the mode
SmartKey Security cylinder you can re-key yourself in seconds
BHMA Grade AAA plus a UL 20-minute fire rating
Geofenced auto-unlock through the Kwikset app
Lifetime mechanical and finish warranty

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: BHMA Grade AAA (Kwikset's published claim), plus a UL 20-minute fire rating. Kwikset publishes the three-letter AAA grade rather than the A156.36 numeric grade
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — but the SmartKey cylinder can be re-keyed by the owner to match an existing key
specs.smartRadio: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Matter over Thread both built in, plus Bluetooth
specs.hubRequired: No hub for Wi-Fi mode. Matter mode needs a Thread border router
specs.appleHomeKey: No — Apple Home Key is only on the dearer Halo Select Plus
specs.backupAccess: SmartKey physical cylinder, owner re-keyable; Kwikset does not publish an emergency power contact
specs.doorFit: Doors 1-3/8 in to 1-3/4 in thick, adjustable 2-3/8 in or 2-3/4 in backset, 2-1/8 in cross bore

pros: Genuinely dual-radio: Wi-Fi for hub-free remote access, or Matter-over-Thread if you already run a Thread mesh
SmartKey lets you re-key the cylinder to your existing house key in under a minute — no locksmith, no new keyring
BHMA Grade AAA and a UL 20-minute fire rating, both published rather than implied
One of the few locks here that states its door thickness, backset and bore limits outright
cons: Matter mode is not a free upgrade: Kwikset's own comparison shows access-code add/remove, code scheduling, event history and door-sensor settings are Kwikset-app-over-Wi-Fi features, not Matter ones
No Apple Home Key — that is a separate, dearer Halo Select Plus SKU
No fingerprint reader at $259 when $200 locks here have one
Kwikset publishes no battery-life figure, and its own product reviews are peppered with Wi-Fi pairing and 'door jammed' complaints
shortTagline: Wi-Fi and Thread in one lock — but choosing Matter costs you code management.

model: Schlage Encode Plus Smart WiFi Deadbolt (BE499WB, Camelot)
material: Solid metal escutcheon with a capacitive touchscreen
features: Published ANSI/BHMA A156.36 Grade 1 and A156.40 Grade AAA
Apple Home Key tap-to-unlock with iPhone or Apple Watch
Built-in Wi-Fi plus Matter over Thread on the same lock
Built-in alarm and time-delayed locking
3-year electronics warranty, lifetime mechanical and finish

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: ANSI/BHMA A156.36 Grade 1 and A156.40 Grade AAA, both named explicitly in Schlage's own security-ratings article — the clearest published grade of any lock in this set
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — new Schlage C-keyway cylinder and keys
specs.smartRadio: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built in, plus Matter certification with Thread
specs.hubRequired: No for the Schlage Home app — Wi-Fi is in the lock. Home Key taps work locally, but remote Apple Home control and Matter need a home hub / Thread border router
specs.appleHomeKey: Yes — tap to unlock with iPhone or Apple Watch
specs.uwbUnlock: No — that is the Sense Pro
specs.batteryClaimMonths: Not published by Schlage for the Encode Plus; owners commonly report 2-6 months, and the lock's Wi-Fi radio is the reason
specs.backupAccess: Keyed cylinder on the Camelot and Century trims; Schlage does not publish an emergency power contact on the Encode Plus
specs.doorFit: Single-bore doors with a 2-3/8 in or 2-3/4 in backset; Schlage does not publish a thickness range on the Encode Plus product page

pros: The only lock here whose maker names both the numeric ANSI grade (A156.36 Grade 1) and the letter grade (A156.40 AAA) in writing
Wi-Fi and Matter-over-Thread together: hub-free remote access from Schlage's app, or Thread if you prefer it
Apple Home Key works as advertised, including on Apple Watch, and the taps are local so they survive an internet outage
3-year electronics warranty against the 1-year most rivals give
cons: Battery life is the weak point — Schlage publishes no figure and owners frequently report 2-3 months on AA cells because the Wi-Fi radio never sleeps for long
No emergency power contact: when the cells die you are using the key, which several cheaper locks here avoid with a USB-C port
No fingerprint reader at $329, when $80 and $200 locks here have one
Physically bulky and unmistakably industrial next to a Level or an Aqara
shortTagline: The rare lock that publishes its Grade 1 rating — and eats AA batteries to do it.

material: Machined metal; Level does not publish the alloy
features: All electronics hidden inside the door — the outside looks like an ordinary deadbolt
ANSI Grade 1/A and BHMA AAA, tested to 250,000 cycles
Apple Home Key plus two NFC key fobs in the box
Integrated door open/closed sensing with no separate magnet
Runs a year on a single CR2 cell hidden inside the bolt

specs.lockType: Full deadbolt replacement with the electronics concealed inside the door
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: ANSI Grade 1/A, tested to A156.40 (residential deadbolts) and A156.25 (electrified locking), BHMA AAA certified at 250,000 cycles — all stated on Level's own page
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — new Level cylinder and keys; your existing key will not work
specs.smartRadio: Matter over Thread plus Bluetooth 4.0/5.0 and NFC. There is no Wi-Fi radio in the lock
specs.hubRequired: Yes — either a Matter-over-Thread hub (HomePod mini, HomePod 2, Apple TV 4K 3rd gen or equivalent) or Level's own Connect Wi-Fi Bridge, sold separately
specs.appleHomeKey: Yes — tap with iPhone or Apple Watch
specs.biometrics: None — and there is no keypad in the box either; the Level Keypad is a separate purchase
specs.batteryType: 1 x CR2 lithium (included), concealed inside the bolt
specs.backupAccess: Two physical keys and two NFC key fobs in the box; there is no emergency power contact, so a flat CR2 means using the key
specs.doorFit: Door thickness 1.75 in to 2.0 in only, backset 2.375 in or 2.75 in, ANSI 2.125 in bore — the narrowest thickness window of any lock here

pros: Genuinely invisible: the only lock here that does not announce itself on the outside or bolt a slab of plastic to the inside
Publishes ANSI Grade 1/A, BHMA AAA and a 250,000-cycle test figure — the security claims are specific and checkable
A single CR2 cell runs it for roughly 9-12 months, so the battery burden is one small cell a year rather than eight AAs
Apple Home Key plus two NFC fobs in the box covers guests who do not have an iPhone
cons: The 1.75-2.0 in door thickness limit is the hard trap: plenty of American doors are 1-3/8 in and simply will not take this lock
No Wi-Fi in the lock — remote access needs either a Thread hub you already own or Level's Connect bridge as an extra purchase
No keypad and no fingerprint in the box; the Level Keypad is another accessory, so out of the box a guest without an iPhone needs a fob or a key
$349 with fewer entry methods than an $80 Wyze, and no emergency power contact when the CR2 dies
shortTagline: Invisible, Grade 1 and beautiful — if your door is between 1.75 and 2 inches thick.

material: Zinc alloy escutcheon with a glass PIN Genie keypad
features: 3D facial recognition with radar approach detection — no camera, no cloud video
0.2s AI fingerprint sensor alongside the face unlock
PIN Genie shuffling keypad defeats shoulder-surfing and finger-smudge attacks
Two 10,000mAh rechargeable packs in the box so one charges while the other runs
Built-in Wi-Fi with no subscription for remote access or history

specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Not published by the manufacturer — Lockly advertises a 5-year mechanical warranty and lifetime support instead of an ANSI/BHMA grade
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — new Lockly cylinder and keys
specs.smartRadio: 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built into the lock. No Matter and no Thread
specs.hubRequired: No — the Wi-Fi radio is in the lock and Lockly charges no subscription for remote access
specs.appleHomeKey: Yes — tap with iPhone or Apple Watch
specs.uwbUnlock: No — approach detection is radar, not UWB, so it recognises a face rather than a phone
specs.biometrics: 3D facial recognition (radar, not a camera) plus a 0.2s AI fingerprint sensor
specs.batteryType: 2 x 10,000mAh rechargeable packs (both included) with a USB-C backup contact
specs.batteryClaimMonths: Sources conflict: Lockly claims up to 8 months per charge, while Tom's Guide found the default settings needed roughly monthly charging
specs.backupAccess: Physical key cylinder, a second charged battery pack you can hot-swap, and a USB-C emergency power contact
specs.doorFit: Standard US single-cylinder deadbolt prep; Lockly does not publish a door-thickness or backset range on the product page

pros: More ways in than anything else here: face, fingerprint, PIN Genie keypad, Apple Home Key, app and a physical key
Face unlock uses radar rather than a camera, so there is no video feed to secure and no cloud storage bill
Two rechargeable packs in the box means you always have a charged spare — no lock in this set handles a flat battery better
Wi-Fi is built in and Lockly charges nothing monthly for remote unlock, codes or history
cons: No published ANSI/BHMA grade at all, at $349 — you cannot compare its physical security to the Grade 1 Schlage or Level
Battery claims do not survive contact with reviewers: Lockly says up to 8 months, Tom's Guide found monthly charging at default settings
No Matter and no Thread, so it is locked to Lockly's cloud for anything beyond Apple Home Key taps and voice assistants
There is no video feed despite the doorbell-like face sensor, which surprises buyers who expect a camera
shortTagline: Face, fingerprint, Home Key and two spare batteries — but no published security grade.

material: Solid metal escutcheon with a capacitive touchscreen
features: Schlage Converge UWB unlocks as you actually walk up, not when your phone is merely nearby
Matter over Thread, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth all on board
Up to 250 access codes and a built-in alarm
Aliro-ready for future Android and Samsung support
Emergency USB-C power contact under the exterior escutcheon

specs.lockType: Full deadbolt replacement, key-free by design
specs.ansiBhmaGrade: Sources conflict: Schlage markets it as an 'AAA Certified Deadbolt', while Tom's Guide and AppleInsider both report ANSI Grade 2. Schlage's own security-ratings article covers only the Encode family and omits Sense Pro
specs.keepsExistingKeyway: No — and there is no exterior keyway at all on this lock
specs.smartRadio: Schlage Converge UWB, Matter over Thread, 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
specs.hubRequired: Yes for remote access and smart-home control — Schlage's own product page states 'Home Hub Required'. The UWB approach-unlock itself is phone-to-lock and needs no hub
specs.appleHomeKey: Yes — tap-to-unlock and hands-free unlock with iPhone and Apple Watch
specs.uwbUnlock: Yes, but iPhone-only today. Schlage says a future Aliro update will bring UWB and NFC to Samsung and other Android devices; that has not shipped
specs.batteryType: Sources conflict: Schlage's product page lists AAA cells, while Tom's Guide and AppleInsider both counted four AA alkalines in the review units
specs.batteryClaimMonths: Schlage claims roughly 6 months on Wi-Fi or 9 months on Thread; Tom's Guide's review unit was down to 51% after two weeks on an unoptimised setup
specs.backupAccess: No physical key cylinder at all. The only fallback is the emergency USB-C port on the underside of the exterior escutcheon
specs.doorFit: Single-bore doors; Schlage does not publish a thickness range for the Sense Pro

pros: UWB approach-unlock genuinely works differently from Bluetooth geofencing — it unlocks when you arrive at the door, not when you are somewhere in the neighbourhood
The most radios of any lock here: UWB, Thread, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, so it fits any ecosystem you already run
Apple Home Key hands-free unlock plus a keypad for guests, with up to 250 codes
Schlage's 3-year electronics warranty and a real emergency USB-C power contact
cons: There is no physical key. If the battery dies and you have no USB-C power bank on you, you are locked out — reviewers call this the dealbreaker
UWB is iPhone-only. The Aliro support that would bring Android and Samsung in is announced, not shipped
Schlage's own page says AAA batteries while two independent reviewers counted four AAs — a basic spec Schlage has not got straight
$399 makes it the most expensive lock here, and the Aqara U400 offers UWB plus a fingerprint reader for around $100 less
shortTagline: The best UWB unlock you can buy, on a lock with no keyhole and disposable AAs.
